newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch launch EU quest game on the Internet.
newsitem.headline: Dutch launch EU quest game on the Internet.

text.p: Saving an imprisoned princess on the Internet from the mythical bull Zeus by answering questions on European affairs and culture is one way in which the Dutch hope to interest their youth in the European Union.

The Dutch, who hold the current EU presidency, unveiled the new game - Quest 4 Europe (www.quest4europe.nl) - on Monday during a two-day EU summit here which amongst other things is looking at how to make the Union more relevant to its citizens.

"The object...is to give young people the opportunity to get acquainted with the Union and the life of other European youngsters in an attractive and interactive way," said the Dutch Europa Centrum. The centre is responsible for informing young people about the EU and was involved in developing the game.
The player has to free the princess - or a prince - who is locked up in a tower by climbing 15 floors, each containing questions of varying difficulty on one EU member state.
The site also has a database of magazines and newspapers which students can refer to for help.

"Editorial imput from young people of the member states, the possibilites for chatting...and an envisaged English translation could turn this temporarily Dutch site into a platform for young people from all member states," the Europa Centrum said.
